t: #3831 Median of a Binary Search Tree Level
o: We need all node values at a given depth, then the upper median of that multiset. Despite being a BST, level membership is a structural question, so BFS (or DFS with depth tracking) is natural — BST ordering alone does not tell you which nodes live at depth L. Once collected, sort the values and return the element at index len//2 (upper median for even sizes). If BFS finishes before reaching the requested depth, or the level exists but is empty, return -1. With up to 2·10^5 nodes, an O(n log n) collect-and-sort is well within limits.
k: Level membership is structural — traverse by depth, don't rely on BST order.
Upper median of a sorted list of size m is simply element at index m//2.
Return -1 when the traversal exhausts before reaching the requested level.

a.i: Process the tree one level at a time; after `level` iterations the queue holds exactly the nodes at that depth. Sort their values and index the upper median. Early-exit once we pass the target depth.
s: Initialize a queue with the root and depth d = 0.
While d < level and the queue is non-empty, expand one full level.
If the queue is empty or d != level afterward, return -1.
Sort the queued values and return vals[len(vals)//2].
a.t: O(n + w log w) — BFS visits each node once; sorting the level of width w dominates.
a.sp: O(w) — the queue holds at most one level.

a.i: Recursively walk the tree carrying the current depth, appending each node's value into a bucket for its depth. Then read bucket[level]. This avoids level-width bookkeeping and is handy when you also need multiple levels' answers.
s: DFS(root, 0): append root.val to buckets[d]; recurse on children with d+1.
If level exceeds the maximum observed depth or the bucket is absent, return -1.
Sort buckets[level] and return the element at index len//2.
a.t: O(n log n) — visiting all nodes plus sorting one bucket (worst case the whole tree is one level).

w: Prefer BFS when only one level is queried (early exit, less memory); DFS-buckets when many queries arrive. Pitfalls: off-by-one on depth (root = level 0), returning the lower median instead of upper for even counts, and forgetting the -1 sentinel for nonexistent levels. A follow-up could ask for the true median of an even-sized level, or answering many level queries after one traversal — the bucket approach generalizes directly.
